purpose: A reading aid, not a test of a rule. Show what followed past days at each level of the published score, finer than the five states.
score: v3_long_score in research/v4/daily.csv (the current rule v3 run over past days, with the long stand-in series)
market: Ken French daily market return (Mkt-RF + RF), the same series and the same outcome definitions as research round 1
period_main: 2007-01-03 to the last day with 63 trading days after it (the same period as the state table on the page)
period_also_reported: 1990-01-02 onward, shown beside the main period so the reader can see whether the picture holds
bins: ten-point bands of the score: 0-9, 10-19, ... 90-100. Fixed before looking at outcomes by band.
per_band: separate spells (runs of consecutive trading days in the band)
share of days followed by a close 10% or more lower within 63 trading days
median of the deepest close within 63 trading days
thin_sample: a band is marked thin when it has fewer than 250 days or fewer than 10 separate spells. Days in a spell are not independent, so the spell count is the honest sample size.
wording: past frequencies, never a probability of a future fall

per_band: share of days by the deepest close within 63 trading days, in four groups fixed here: less than 5% down, 5% to under 10%, 10% to under 20%, 20% or more
for days followed by a 10% fall: median trading days until the first close 10% or more lower
addendum_2026-11-27_outcome_mix.forward_check: These are past frequencies. From the first record (2026-11-26) the published score and what followed will be compared with these shares in public; first review after 12 months of records. Until then nothing here is called a forecast.
